identity.title: Dust masses of young disks: constraining the initial solid reservoir for planet formation

paper_type_evidence.quote: In this paper we analyze ALMA Band 6 continuum observations of 44 protostars in the Perseus molecular cloud.

evidence.quote: The average spatial resolution of observations ($0.38\ensuremath{''}$) corresponds to 110 au (diameter) at the distance to Perseus (293$\pm 22$ pc; (cite: Ortiz-Leon2018)).

question.value: Do embedded Class 0/I disks in Perseus contain enough dust to explain the solid content of the most massive exoplanets, and what efficiency is needed?

evidence.quote: We aim to determine if disks in the embedded stage of star formation contain enough dust to explain the solid content of the most massive exoplanets.
The data were obtained in September 2018 with a Cycle 5 program (2017.1.01693.S, PI: T. Hsieh).
Additional data on 8 disks were obtained in a Cycle 5 program (2017.1.01078.S, PI: D. Segura-Cox).

analysis_steps.goal: measure disk fluxes with Gaussian fits

method.value: imfit with compact Gaussian plus optional broad 3" envelope Gaussian; compact component taken as disk

evidence.quote: The CASA (cite: McMullin2007) v. 5.4.0 $\it imfit$ task was used to fit Gaussian profiles to the sources.

key_parameters.value: Envelope Gaussian added in 31 of 51 targets; initial broad size 3"

evidence.quote: an additional broad Gaussian with a size of 3$''$ was added to the initial guess parameters of the fitting

assumptions.value: Compact Gaussian flux equals disk flux

evidence.quote: The flux density of the compact Gaussian is assumed to be that of the embedded disk.

fitting.value: all Gaussian parameters free; size fixed to beam in two sources

evidence.quote: In two cases (Per-emb-4 and SVS13A2) it was necessary to fix the size of the Gaussian to the synthesized beam size for the fit to converge

validation.value: Residual envelope flux measured in residual images; inspected by eye

evidence.quote: All sources were inspected by eye to assess the number of necessary Gaussian components.

analysis_steps.goal: compare ALMA and VLA fluxes and derive spectral index and beta

method.value: Linear fit of fluxes with lmfit; alpha between 1 mm and 9 mm; beta = (alpha-2)(1+Delta); optically thin subsample where alpha_VLA/ALMA - alpha_VLA <= 0.4

evidence.loc: Comparison of the integrated fluxes between 1 and 9 mm
evidence.quote: There is a clear correlation with a close-to-linear slope (1.15 $\pm$ 0.10) obtained with the *lmfit* Python function.

evidence.loc: Comparison of the integrated fluxes between 1 and 9 mm
evidence.quote: in which case $\Delta$ = 0 and then $\beta = \alpha - 2$.

validation.value: Optical depth estimated from deconvolved major axis: tau < 0.4

evidence.loc: Comparison of the integrated fluxes between 1 and 9 mm
evidence.quote: For all the disks with available major axis value, we get $\tau < 0.4$ and in vast majortiy of cases $<0.1$.

method.value: M = D^2 F / (kappa B(T)), T=30 K; CDFs with survival analysis including upper limits; medians at 0.5 probability

evidence.quote: Temperature of the dust is set to 30 K, typical for dust in dense protostellar envelopes (cite: Whitney2003), and disks are assumed to be isothermal.

key_parameters.value: kappa_9mm = 0.28 cm2/g (DIANA); kappa_1.3mm = 2.3 cm2/g; for Orion comparison kappa_1.3mm = 0.9

evidence.quote: Here we adopt $\kappa_{9 {\rm mm}}= 0.28 \ {\rm cm^{2}\ g^{-1}}$ as provided by dust models of the DIANA project
$\kappa_\nu$ is the dust opacity with the assumption of optically thin emission.

validation.value: VLA sample complete, ALMA ~80% complete so VLA medians more reliable

evidence.quote: While the VLA observations sample is complete, the ALMA sample of disks is not, as we assemble $\sim 80\%$ of the total sample.

analysis_steps.goal: compare to exoplanet solids and derive formation efficiency

method.value: Exoplanet systems (>=1 planet >0.3 MJ) normalized to 18% of population; solid mass via Thorngren2016; efficiency = ratio of exoplanet to disk dust mass at same CDF level

evidence.loc: Comparison of young disk dust masses with the solids in exoplanetary systems
evidence.quote: The efficiency is calculated as a ratio of the total mass of the exoplanetary systems at the certain fraction of the cumulative distribution plot divided by the corresponding dust mass of the disk at the same value of the CDF plot.

key_parameters.value: 0.3 MJ planet solid fraction 27.8 Mearth set at 18% of CDF

evidence.quote: This is done by setting the 18% value of the CDF plot at the estimated solid fraction of the gaseous planet of 0.3 M$_{\rm J}$, which is 27.8 M$_{\oplus}$.
The CASA (cite: McMullin2007) v. 5.4.0 $\it imfit$ task was used to fit Gaussian profiles to the sources.

evidence.loc: Comparison of the integrated fluxes between 1 and 9 mm
evidence.quote: obtained with the *lmfit* Python function

findings_qualitative.value: Class 0 disks are more massive in Perseus than in Orion; Class I similar

evidence.quote: while disk masses in Class I disks agree well, Class 0 disks are more massive in Perseus than in Orion.

claims.hypothesis: Emission at 1 mm and 9 mm is dust-dominated and indicates grain growth
claims.experiment: Compared ALMA and VLA fluxes and spectral indices
claims.result: Slope 1.15±0.10; alpha~2.5 for optically thin subsample, beta~0.5
claims.finding: Dust emission dominates both; significant grain growth

evidence.quote: A strong linear correlation between the ALMA and VLA fluxes is observed, demonstrating that emission at both wavelengths is dominated by dust emission.

claims.hypothesis: Young disks hold more dust than Class II disks
claims.experiment: Computed medians and compared with Lupus
claims.result: Class 0 and I masses higher by at least factors 10 and 3

evidence.quote: The dust masses of young Class 0 and I disks are larger by at least a factor of 10 and 3, respectively, compared with dust masses inferred for Class II disks in Lupus and other regions.

claims.hypothesis: Embedded disks contain enough solids to form observed giant exoplanets
claims.experiment: Compared disk mass CDF with exoplanet solid mass CDF
claims.finding: Planet formation can start in Class 0/I with acceptable efficiency

evidence.quote: the solid content in observed giant exoplanets can be explained if planet formation starts in Class 0 phase with an efficiency of $\sim$ 15%.

evidence.quote: The way forward is to use observations of young disks with VLA and ALMA in the same star-forming region
